Thanks for the time. Let us start with the balance sheet reconciliation. How is it approved?
It is prepared by the analyst, reviewed by the accounting manager, and signed off before the fifth working day. The review is the internal control.
Good. And what happens if the reviewer finds a difference?
Anything above materiality is escalated to the manager the same day. Below that, it is listed and cleared in the following month.
Understood. We selected a sample of forty entries last week. Is the supporting documentation kept with the working paper, or somewhere else?
With the working paper. Every balance above the threshold is substantiated, and the invoice is attached in the same folder.

A short note for anybody who has never been through an audit with me. There is one habit that turns a two-day request into a two-week request, and it is not a technical one. It is answering a question about a process by talking about a person. When I ask how the reconciliation is approved, and somebody tells me that Ana does it, I now have two questions instead of one, because I still do not know what happens when Ana is on holiday. Tell me the process, not the person. The reconciliation is prepared by the analyst, reviewed by the manager, and signed off before the fifth working day. Now I know what the control is, and I can test it. If you want to shorten an audit, that one sentence is worth more than any spreadsheet you send me.

The first year I led the audit, I answered every question with everything I knew, and it made things worse. Somebody would ask a simple question about one account and I would give them eight minutes of context, and by the end they had four new questions, all of them about things they had not been looking at. What I do now is much shorter, and it took me three closings to learn it. I answer the question that was asked. I say where the evidence is. And then I stop talking, and I let them decide whether they want more. If they do, they will ask. And if I do not know the answer, I say so, I say who does, and I say when it will reach them. That is the whole method. It sounds small, and it is the difference between an audit that ends in March and one that ends in May.
